items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And there was a lot of experimental music. Dave Liebman came out of that and Richie Bierach

ctx.x: Years later you played on a record of hers I have — “Ambiance?” There was some pretty adventurous playing on that.

Yeah well Marian and I talked about that recently, and three or four of my tunes were on there, and they were pretty avante garde. I was kind of in that era of player at the time, and Marian, always wanting to be young musically and keep up with what’s going on, surrounded herself with young players and wanted to get into what they were into. But it’s funny, after that, with me I kind of spent my time in that group of people, like we had a space, it was called The Space, and it was a bunch of musicians and we all…
It’s always been a struggle with that kind of music, as far as your audience reception to it I think. I don’t know if after a while you say maybe this isn’t valid for anyone except myself perhaps.
